sentences.text: 1 factum of pregnancy was disclosed.
Twins were born to the victim, but the accused applicant refused to accept them or to give any maintenance for the same.
The incident started 6 years prior to the lodging of the F.I.R.
On 27.8.2023, the F.I.R. was lodged and investigation started and now charge-sheet has been submitted.

6. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and he has apprehension of his arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against him.
He has been falsely implicated into this matter.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
The investigation of the case has been completed and charge-sheet has been filed.
It is also submitted that F.I.R. has been lodged 6 years after the incident without any plausible explanation of delay.
It is also submitted that there is absolutely no proof of the fact at this stage that the present applicant is the father of the children given birth by the victim.
It is also submitted that the victim never protested or made complaint regarding the sexual exploitation said to be made by the applicant with her.

It is also submitted that there was some prior dispute between the applicant and the family of the informant and a compromise had also taken place in this regard prior to the lodging of the present F.I.R., but subsequently, money was demanded by the informant side and when it was refused, F.I.R. was lodged on the basis of false allegations.
It is also submitted that the applicant has been cooperative during the course of investigation.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal history to his credit and as such he is entitled for anticipatory bail.

7. It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that the anticipatory bail application of the applicant was rejected by the Sessions Court at Chaudauli on 7.10.2023 and on 9.10.2023,
non-bailable warrant was issued against the applicant in a very hasty manner.

It is also submitted that process under section 82 Cr.P.C. was issued under the instructions on 20.10.2023 and on the very next day i.e. 21.10.2023, process under section 83 Cr.P.C. was also issued by the Court against the applicant.
The applicant moved anticipatory bail application before this Court on 27.10.2023.

It is vehemently submitted that the whole proceedings of the Magistrate Court in issuance of punitive process against the applicant are arbitrary and against the law and the applicant cannot be termed as a proclaimed offender and he cannot be denied the benefit of anticipatory bail on this ground.
8.

On the other hand, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and submitted that undoubtedly, the victim of this case was a minor girl at the time of initiation of her sexual exploitation by the present applicant, who made physical relations with the victim several times and consent, if any, given by the victim has no legal value at all.

It is also submitted that in the F.I.R., it has been specifically mentioned that in April 2022, the victim got pregnancy out of the physical relations made by the applicant with her and thereafter she got married with one Mukesh Kumar in May 2022.

It is also submitted that it is a shameful aspect of the matter that the victim also gave birth to twins out of the physical relations made by the applicant, which was a social stigma for the poor victim.
It is also submitted that the applicant is a proclaimed offender and his anticipatory bail application is not maintainable.

It is also submitted that there was some previous dispute between the two families and a compromise had also taken place between the two, but that was not the cause for lodging of the F.I.R. in this matter.
It is also submitted that on the basis of high school marks-sheet of the victim, her age in 2017 i.e. 6 years prior to the lodging of the F.I.R. was less than 18 years and she was a minor girl.

sentences.text: In the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the factum of sexual exploitation of the minor victim by the present accused applicant, this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.

Ample evidence has been collected against the applicant during investigation and thereafter charge-sheet has been submitted and cognizance has been taken on 14.12.2023 against the applicant as an absconder.
It is a case of fulfilling of lust by the applicant with a minor girl, whose consent, if any, has no legal value in the eye of law.
The applicant has not been cooperative during the course of investigation and that is why punitive processes were issued against him by the Court.

10. Hence, considering the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation,
role of applicant, gravity of the offence and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, it is not a fit case for anticipatory bail to the applicant.
11. The anticipatory bail application is, accordingly, rejected.
